posts.author: Kinmizu
posts.body:
shiroisekai said:
hello everyone, i wanna make my character 16x16 is there a template to do it? i just want to have a 1 character template and also what naming should i put if i were to use galvs plugin character frames plugin?
Click to expand...
Dear friend. Good day to you. Assuming you are using: MZ or MV. The grid is 48p x - y per cell. sheets are 576 x 384.  With 12 character column followed by 8 variation. Assuming also that you know that already.
Now, dividing them gives 24 by 24 grid for your character on which you can draw 16 x 16. hence you get the same result 12 character by 8 with more blank space per cell. The major problem now is the grid movement which remains 48px. Character movement appears to have a jump instead of walk. so i understand you use galv script we will talk later. unless you divide your sheet by 2 = 288 x 192 and you have to rename the sheet properly. Because the DEV must include code/functions so that the engine knows what you are doing. These are often defined by Sign Keys or variable. I do not know if this is defined automatically by the engine itself, here!, I am very sorry. I do not use rpg maker MZ and i can't test this at present to be sure. Otherwise there are proper renaming that you have to put like for example a '$, @ sign or %' in front of name. Eg of Sheet name:" %mycharacter1" where mycharacter1 can be %shiro or %anythingyoulike. you will have to search for the proper abbreviation.
on tiles you will have to use either parallax mapping or you will have to set it correctly so that the character appear to be walking on 24x 24 grid. With modern screen a 16 by 16 character can walk 24 tiles. Long ago CRT screen were not flat and the loop/lens was in the middle which makes things appear bigger at the center. Settings must have been 90% accurate for sprites without mentioning the lines... Nowadays, this problem is solved. If you are still using the default 48 cell 576 x 384 you have noticed that your space/gap will be wider between frames. If you draw the character close enough you will see 2 or 3 variation of the character in the same column. And the animation is broken. This is because you have not tell the engine by the language that he understands that you have change your character size.
If you persist need 16 by 16 and you own engines like VXAce or rpg maker 2003 they are the best options. in VX A the tiles are 32 and when divided they give 16 which is perfect. you only need the grid movement changed by half, again this is script call or pluggin already made by friendly game Dev. However if you still want the more modern RPG MZ I can understand because it gives plenty of options.
Return to Galv script. Galv usually provide demo along in the description or download link, it is very helpful to download his demo in order to access the root files and understand how his project works. These files are included to simplify your understanding with a fun experience. You get all the details on how things should be properly set up and being named. Just open the documents which contains his character and see how he has named them and set. Do the same with your project. If it works, say thank you to Galv and on you go continue making your project. If that answers your question, I wish you a nice day and happy game making if not I apology.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Kinmizu said:
Assuming you are using: MZ or MV. The grid is 48p x - y per cell. sheets are 576 x 384.  With 12 character column followed by 8 variation. Assuming also that you know that already.
Now, dividing them gives 24 by 24 grid for your character on which you can draw 16 x 16. hence you get the same result 12 character by 8 with more blank space per cell.
Click to expand...
This is not correct.
Per the instructions in Help -> Contents -> Documentation -> Asset Standards, the cel sizes can be any dimensions you want. They do not have to be 48x48 and they do not have to be square.
Only the numbers of cels per row and the numbers of row are required (and that's where the instructions for the Galv plugin must be looked at).
This has been true at least as far back as VX. You can copy a character sheet from VX to MZ or
vice versa
and they will display/be selectable perfectly in the editor.
shiroisekai said:
i wanna make my character 16x16 is there a template to do it?
Click to expand...
Just go into the image editor you're using and tell it to display a grid in whatever dimensions you want.
